batch.loan_advance_repayment.why: loanAdvanceRepayment settles overdue installments from a loan's excess_amount by calling the internal loanRepayment API per row (LoanAdvanceRepaymentItemWriter.java:64), with a reversal fallback on failure at :66. It writes nothing itself. A drain assert was written first and REMOVED after the run disproved it. The reader's WHERE clause (excess_amount > 0 with an unsettled installment due) returned exactly 1 candidate, account 8161861 / 6004113526 carrying 10276.00. The job read 1, wrote 1 and reported COMPLETED - and excess_amount is still 10276.00, with no client_request_response_log row for that account today and no batch_failure_audit row for the job. So the account was processed and the money did not move, and nothing anywhere records why. That may be a legitimate business rejection inside loanRepayment; it may not. Either way the drain is not this job's contract, so asserting it would have shipped a red that means nothing. Liveness until the single local candidate is explained. Note this job is one of the four GAP-093 exposures - LoanAdvanceRepaymentFailureEntityMapper chain-dereferences the skip item and the job runs force_async=TRUE - so a writer-side item failure here would fail the whole job and record nothing. It did not fail this run.

This case was first tagged service, which under-gated it. This case asserts that it RAN and processed the population - read 2057 / write 2057 across 10 partitions - and nothing about the resulting state, deliberately. Those 3472 rows are worth resolving - either the dues rows are legitimately left unsettled at closure, in which case the invariant needs the real outstanding source, or the fixture is dirty. Until then this case is a liveness check and says so.

This case drives the REAL initiate leg (function_code=DEFAULT, run_mode=REAL) over HTTP against a freshly disbursed LAN and audits the row it writes. WHY THE ASSERT IS NOT DECORATIVE: every money field on loan_disbursement_cancellation_details is copied verbatim from the request - CreateDisbursementCancellationDetailsProcessor.populateBpiDetailsData sets bpi_amount from request bpi_details.due_amount and populatePrincipalOutstandingDetailsData sets principal_outstanding_amount from principal_outstanding_details.amount_to_be_paid. The only validator in front of them, ValidateDisbursementCancellationAmountDetails, checks INTERNAL ARITHMETIC ONLY (sum of amount_to_be_paid + round_off - excess - cross_sell + exclusive tax - deducted charges == total_cancellation_amount, plus waiver self-consistency at 134315/134316/134317). Nothing compares the submitted principal or BPI against what the system itself computes and showed the borrower in fetchDisbursementCancellationSimulationDetails. CLAUSES, each returning the OFFENDING VALUE: (1) NO_CANCELLATION_ROW - initiate reported SUCCESS and wrote nothing. (2) LOAN_NOT_FROZEN - updateLoanAccountStatusProcessor did not move the loan to DISB_CNCL_FREEZE, so a cancelling loan stays collectable. (3) TASK_STATE - cancellation_status/task_status not PENDING/PENDING. (4) CANCEL_DATE_AFTER_FIRST_EMI - guards the window ValidateDataForDisbursementCancellation.java:107 enforces, and is also the precondition that makes clause 6 valid. (5) PRIN_OUTSTANDING_MISMATCH - the persisted principal must equal LoanDueDetailsRepository.getFuturePrincipalOutstandingAmount (SUM(due_amount-paid_amount-waived_amount) over PRIN rows with due_date > cancellation_date, is_deleted=false), mirrored exactly. (6) BPI_SPLIT_MISMATCH - bpi_amount must equal bpi_amount_to_be_paid + bpi_waived_amount, so a waiver cannot be hidden inside the headline figure. (7) BPI_OFF_ACCRUAL - the submitted BPI must be within 1.00 of outstanding_principal * effective_rate/100 * days/360, capped at the first INT installment due. That is InterestCalculationUtil.calculateInterestTillDateUsingReducingBalance for the pre-first-EMI window - the only window this API can serve - which ends in .min(currentInstallment.getDueAmount()). The 1.00 band is deliberate: the Java path applies roundAmountWithPrecision with the product installmentRoundingFactor, which is a rounding ARTIFACT, not a contract, so exact equality would produce false failures. (8) EXCESS_MISMATCH and (9) CROSS_SELL_MISMATCH - the excess and cross-sell credited against the cancellation must equal what the loan actually holds (loan_account.excess_amount / cross_sell_amount, NULL treated as zero); a phantom excess reduces what the borrower is asked to pay. batch.trial_balance_zeroisation.why: trialBalanceZeroisationJob. Uses a MIDNIGHT job_time, and that is not a workaround - it is what production passes. The platform business date (current.business.date) is midnight-stamped; the workspace's default JOB_TIME correlator is 18:00 IST, which no production caller ever supplies. A same-day claim that this job cannot pass its own gate was WITHDRAWN after checking that: the cron controls when the job is triggered, not the job_time parameter it receives. trialBalanceZeroisationJob is two tasklets, no reader/writer, so batch_step_execution read/write counts are 0 even on a fully successful run - they cannot tell a real run from a no-op, and the job returns HTTP 200 + COMPLETED either way. Only the SQL proof separates them. SEED (both statements, and both must be restored afterwards): UPDATE mfi_accounting.trial_balance_run_history SET tb_last_run_date='2027-03-31', is_zeroisation_done=NULL WHERE id=503; and an opening_balance row for the new FY: INSERT INTO mfi_accounting.opening_balance (gl_code, office_id, external_branch_code, opening_balance, financial_year, created_by, created_on, updated_by, updated_on, opening_balance_after_zeroisation) VALUES ('47631', 1, '', 28512.000000, '2027-04-01 00:00:00', 'SYSTEM', now(), 'SYSTEM', now(), NULL) -- guard with NOT EXISTS. RESTORE AFTER THE RUN: UPDATE ... SET tb_last_run_date='2026-06-26', is_zeroisation_done=NULL WHERE id=503 - row 503 is the CURRENT financial year row (2026-04-01..2027-03-31) and is the same row PopulateTrialBalanceBatchTasklet walks from for batch.trial_balance_calc, so leaving the seeded value in place makes that case calculate nothing. The two cases cannot share the fixture; the seed is temporary by construction. WHY THE SEED IS NEEDED: validateJobRundate (TrialBalanceZeroisationBatchService.java:109-133) runs the job only when the business date is April 1, the run-history row keyed on the previous FY's last day exists, its tb_last_run_date is not before that day, and is_zeroisation_done is not already true. Without the opening_balance row the first tasklet posts nothing and any assert passes vacuously. JOB_TIME MUST BE MIDNIGHT (1806517800000 = 2027-04-01 00:00 IST). tb_last_run_date is a DATE column, so the entity value is always midnight, while lastDayOfPreviousFinancialYear carries job_time's time-of-day. At the recipe's 18:00 job_time (1806582600000) the comparison is 2027-03-31 00:00 .before(2027-03-31 18:00) = true and the job terminates with 'TB: Not calculated for the last day of previous Financial Year' - observed, and the job's own cron is '0 0 18 * * ?', so in production this gate can only pass if the trigger lands exactly at 00:00:00.000. Flagged as a behaviour, not worked around. RED: with the seed applied and the 18:00 job_time the job returned HTTP 200, reached COMPLETED in 1s, wrote nothing, and db_eq returned MISMATCH. GREEN: with the midnight job_time the job posted exactly two legs - 47631 (INCOME) DR 28512.000000 office 1 and 230200001 (retail earning, config retail.earning.gl.code) CR 28512.000000 office 1, is_child_gl_code=false, net zero - and db_eq returned SUCCESS. An immediate second run without the reseed returned COMPLETED again and db_eq MISMATCH, which is the assert proving it is fail-closed: it is scoped by transaction_master.stan = the STAN ntest generated for THIS run, so a no-op writes no matching master row and cannot pass on rows a previous run left. NOT VERIFIED: the second tasklet's opening_balance.opening_balance_after_zeroisation leg. PopulateOpeningBalanceAfterZeroisationBatchTasklet reads its own postings back with 'transaction_details WHERE business_date = firstDayOfFY', but CreateTransactionMasterProcessor.java:72 stamps business_date from platformDateUtil.getBusinessDateInLong() - the platform business date, which on this local stack is 2025-12-04, not 2027-04-01. The readback therefore matched nothing, no opening_balance row was updated, and the tasklet still set is_zeroisation_done=true, so the leg is lost silently and the job cannot be retried without a manual reset. In production the two dates coincide because the job runs at BOD on April 1; the coupling is undocumented and is a candidate gap. Proving that leg locally needs the platform business date moved to 2027-04-01, which is a global masterdata config (current.business.date) that every other registry case depends on - not moved.

(SELECT o.excess_amount FROM orig o))::text WHEN (SELECT COALESCE(r.dpi_amount, 0) FROM rev r) <> (SELECT COALESCE(o.dpi_amount, 0) FROM orig o) THEN 'REVERSAL_SPLIT_MISMATCH:dpi:' || ((SELECT COALESCE(r.dpi_amount, 0) FROM rev r) - offenders: QUEUE_NOT_DRAINED:<status> / QUEUE_ERROR:<msg> - ChildLoanEventProcessingItemProcessor swallows the exception into filler_1 and leaves event_status P, so a failed reversal is silent without this clause
DUE_PAID_NOT_RESTORED:<due_id>=<delta>,... - per row. A reversal that unwinds the right TOTAL off the wrong installments reports both offending rows
OFFSETTING_PAYMENT_ROWS:<n> - not exactly one R_<ref> row (0 = no back-out, 2 = double reversal)
REVERSAL_SPLIT_MISMATCH:<component>:<delta> - offsetting row total right, component split wrong

acceptance.note: The per-row baseline is captured by the script before the repayment and rendered into the SQL as a VALUES list - the DB keeps no appropriation history, so a self-contained query cannot know the pre-repayment values. Per-row restoration is a contract only while the reversed repayment is the only unreversed one on those rows: RepaymentReversalDataGenerator walks paid due rows by loan_installment_details_id DESC and unwinds greedily per component, while repayment appropriates oldest-first, so with several outstanding repayments the reversal can legitimately unwind a different row set. The scenario repays once, then reverses, which is where the invariant holds exactly. dpi_amount is compared NULL-safely and is expected to be NULL on both rows: no code on mfi_integration_v3.4.2.5 writes it (grep setDpiAmount across trustt-platform-accounting/src/main/java returns nothing), so asserting it strictly would be a vacuous check today and a live one when the DPI train lands.

ldd.loan_account_id WHERE ldd.is_deleted = false ), paud AS ( SELECT w.identifier_value, SUM(w.waived_amount) AS parent_waived FROM mfi_accounting.waiver__loan_due_details w JOIN pdue ON pdue.id = w.loan_due_details_id WHERE w.identifier_type = 'WAIVER' GROUP BY 1 ), caud AS ( SELECT w.identifier_value, SUM(w.waived_amount) AS child_waived FROM mfi_accounting.waiver__loan_due_details w JOIN kdue ON kdue.id = w.loan_due_details_id WHERE w.identifier_type = 'WAIVER' GROUP BY 1 ) SELECT COALESCE( (SELECT 'WAIVER_AUDIT_NOT_APPLIED_TO_DUE:ldd=' || kdue.id || ' child_loan_account_id=' || paud.parent_waived || ' child_sum=' || COALESCE(caud.child_waived, 0) FROM paud LEFT JOIN caud ON caud.identifier_value = paud.identifier_value WHERE COALESCE(caud.child_waived, -1) <> waived_amount=' || kdue.waived_amount FROM kdue JOIN aud ON aud.ldd_id = kdue.id WHERE kdue.paid_amount + kdue.waived_amount > kdue.due_amount ORDER BY kdue.id LIMIT 1), CASE WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM kids) = 0 THEN 'NO_CHILDREN_FOR_PARENT' WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM paud) = 0 THEN 'NO_PARENT_WAIVER_AUDIT_ROWS' WHEN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM aud) = 0 THEN 'NO_CHILD_WAIVER_AUDIT_ROWS' ELSE 'SUCCESS' END)

acceptance.note: The audited quantity is loan_due_details.waived_amount, NOT a reduction in due_amount: UpdateLoanDueDetailsForWaiverProcessor:37-39 does waived_amount += waiverAmount and never touches due_amount. Parent->child split is GroupLoanUtility.distributeAmountsEqually, which is exact (the last child absorbs the rounding difference), so the parent/child parity clause carries no tolerance. That split is EQUAL per child, not pro rata to each child's own due, so a parent waiver larger than n * (smallest child pending) can legitimately push one child over its due - the driver sizes the waiver inside that headroom.
